what_happened: Reason code AC01 means the beneficiary's bank could not use the IBAN, either because its format is invalid or because it does not exist at that bank. The payment was rejected before settlement, so no money moved. The likely causes are an invalid IBAN from the beneficiary, wrong IBAN data from the customer's records, or a technical problem when the instruction was created.
next_step: Route to Platform support (FIRST_LINE) to resolve with the customer. Support should ask the customer to confirm the beneficiary's correct IBAN with the beneficiary and provide it, then decide how to proceed. The scheme suggests the originator obtains the correct IBAN from the beneficiary.
customer_message: Your instant transfer was rejected because the beneficiary account number (IBAN) could not be used by the beneficiary's bank. No money was taken from your account for this payment. Please check the beneficiary's IBAN with the beneficiary and contact our support team with the correct details.

what_happened: AC04 means the beneficiary's account is closed at the beneficiary's bank, so the payment was rejected before settlement and no money moved. It most often happens because the beneficiary closed the account after the customer last paid them.
next_step: Route to Platform support (FIRST_LINE) to resolve with the customer. The suggested step under the scheme rule is for the customer to contact the beneficiary to obtain their new account details. Note that some SEPA countries send MS03 instead of AC04 for the same situation.
customer_message: Your instant transfer was not completed because the recipient's account could not be found as open at their bank. No money has left your account. You may wish to contact the recipient to confirm their current account details before sending the payment again.

what_happened: AC06 means the beneficiary's bank has blocked the beneficiary's account for transactions, so the SEPA Instant payment was rejected before settlement and no money moved. The block may be due to a court order or a block placed by the beneficiary's bank, for example on suspicion of misuse or at the beneficiary's request.
next_step: Route to Platform support (first line) to resolve with the customer. Per the scheme guidance, the customer should contact the beneficiary to agree an alternative account or another way to pay. The cause of the block is not visible to us, so do not speculate about it with the customer.
customer_message: Your instant transfer was not completed because the recipient's bank has blocked the recipient's account for transactions. No money has left your account. Please contact the recipient to agree an alternative account or another way to pay.

what_happened: AG01 means the SEPA Instant payment was rejected before settlement because this transaction type is not allowed on the account, usually because the beneficiary's details point to an account that cannot receive SCT Inst payments. No money moved. Route is FIRST_LINE, so platform support resolves it with the customer.
next_step: Platform support should contact the customer to confirm the beneficiary account details and agree with the customer on another payment method, such as a standard SEPA credit transfer. Re-initiating as a standard transfer is only possible if the customer and our bank agreed this beforehand, subject to applicable law. This follows the scheme guidance in KB-SCTI-AG01-01, not team guidance.
customer_message: Your instant payment could not be completed because this type of transaction is not allowed on the account involved. No money has been taken from your account. Please contact us so we can help you agree on another way to send the payment to the beneficiary.

what_happened: AM05 means the clearing system or the beneficiary's bank treated this SEPA Instant payment as a duplicate of an identical payment sent or processed very recently, so it was stopped before settlement and no money moved. The EPC names technical or human error at the originator or originator's bank as the root cause.
next_step: Route to DEVELOPER (technical or system issue). Check with the originator and its bank whether the payment was really duplicated, and look for a technical or system fault on our side that could have sent the same payment twice.
customer_message: Your recent instant transfer was not completed because the system flagged it as a possible duplicate of a payment sent very recently. No money has left your account. We are looking into what happened, and we will contact you if we need anything from you.

what_happened: AB05 means the beneficiary's bank did not receive or process this SEPA Instant payment within the scheme time limit. The payment was rejected before settlement, so no money moved. The cause may lie anywhere between our bank, the clearing system and the beneficiary's bank.
next_step: Platform support should resolve this with the customer, as set by the routing table. Confirm the payment did not settle, then advise the customer that re-sending later or using a standard SEPA credit transfer is an option, per the scheme guidance.
customer_message: Your instant payment did not go through because it was not received by the beneficiary's bank in time. No money was taken from your account for this payment. You can try sending it again later, or use a standard SEPA credit transfer instead. You may also want to check with the beneficiary about another way to pay.

what_happened: MS02 means the beneficiary refused this SEPA Instant payment at presentation and gave no reason. The beneficiary's bank acted on the beneficiary's own instruction, so no funds moved (stage REJECT). The reason is withheld on purpose and should not be guessed.
next_step: Route to Platform support (FIRST_LINE) to resolve with the customer. Per the scheme's suggested step, the customer may contact the beneficiary directly to agree how to settle any amount owed. Team guidance: do not speculate about the reason or contact the beneficiary's bank for it.
customer_message: Your instant payment was not completed because the recipient's bank declined it and did not give a reason. No money was taken from your account. You may wish to contact the recipient directly to discuss the payment. If you need help, please contact our support team.

what_happened: MS03 means the beneficiary's bank rejected the payment without a specific reason, which the EPC permits only where national law such as data-protection law forbids a more precise code. The underlying cause could be a closed account or a regulatory reason, and no money moved because the payment was rejected before settlement.
next_step: Route to Platform support (FIRST_LINE) to resolve with the customer. Per the EPC scheme rule, the originator can contact the beneficiary directly to agree how to settle the obligation; this is a suggestion for the operations agent to confirm, not a decision.
customer_message: Your instant transfer was not completed because the receiving bank did not give a reason for rejecting it. No money has left your account. Please contact the person or company you were paying to agree how to settle the payment.

what_happened: RR04 on a SEPA Instant reject means the beneficiary's bank stopped the payment for a regulatory reason, typically a potential AML, embargo or counter-terrorist-financing hit. We are the payer's bank; no money moved (REJECT stage). Route is COMPLIANCE, so this is for the compliance team to review.
next_step: Hand to Compliance. Do not contact the customer about the reason; Compliance decides what, if anything, is said.

what_happened: AC01 means the debtor's IBAN was invalid in format or does not exist at the debtor's bank. This is a return after settlement, so the funds moved and came back. Our customer is the creditor, so the fix is on the collection data side: the cause may be wrong debtor data, wrong IBAN data from the customer's records, or a technical problem on the collection.
next_step: Route to Platform support, who resolve this with the customer. Per the scheme rule, the customer should contact the debtor to obtain the correct IBAN, and if the mandate was amended, check the data the debtor provided.
customer_message: A direct debit you collected was returned because the account number (IBAN) on it could not be matched to an account at the payer's bank. Please check the IBAN in your records and, if needed, contact the payer to confirm the correct IBAN before collecting again.

what_happened: AC04 means the debtor's account was closed at the debtor's bank, usually after the debtor's last collection from that account. Here the direct debit was settled and then returned, so the funds were refunded to the payer. Under the SDD scheme, the suggested creditor action is to contact the debtor for their new account; some SEPA countries send MS03 instead of AC04 for the same situation.
next_step: Platform support should work with the customer (creditor) to contact the debtor and obtain a new account for future collections, as the scheme suggests. If the code later appears as MS03, treat it as an unspecified reason and still contact the debtor, since the cause could be a closed account, insufficient funds, or other issues. (Team guidance: this is the first-line route in the routing table.)
customer_message: A direct debit you collected from a payer was returned because the payer's account has been closed. To keep collecting payments, please contact the payer to ask for their current account details.

what_happened: AC06 means the debtor's account, or this particular collection, is blocked, so the direct debit was returned after settlement and the funds came back to the debtor. The block may be a court order or a block placed by the debtor's bank, which we cannot see from this case. Route is FIRST_LINE, so platform support handles it with the customer.
next_step: Platform support should contact the customer (creditor) to discuss an alternative way to collect, such as another account or payment method, and confirm whether the debtor's bank block is still in place before any new collection. Note that the creditor's bank can take such actions on the creditor's behalf only where this has been agreed. This is a suggestion from the scheme rule, not team guidance.
customer_message: A direct debit you collected was returned because the payer's account is blocked for this payment. Our team can help you look at other ways to collect the payment, such as using a different account or payment method. Please contact your platform support team so we can go through the options with you.

what_happened: AG01 means the direct debit was forbidden on the debtor's account for regulatory reasons, such as the debtor having given the details of a savings account. The money moved and was returned after settlement (SDD return). We are the creditor's bank, so the issue sits on the debtor's side of the collection.
next_step: Platform support should resolve this with the customer (FIRST_LINE route). Support can ask the customer to contact the debtor to agree on another payment account or payment instrument. If this is an SDD B2B collection presented to a consumer account, the EPC rule says AC13 should have been used instead of AG01, so check the collection type before closing.
customer_message: A direct debit you collected was returned because the payer's account cannot be used for this type of payment. Please contact the payer to agree on another payment account or payment method.

what_happened: AM04 means the debtor's account did not hold enough funds to cover the collection, and the payment was returned after settlement, so the money moved and came back. Per the EPC, a creditor-side root cause can also be missing or late pre-notification of the collection date and amount.
next_step: Route to Platform support (FIRST_LINE) to resolve with the customer, per the routing table. Suggested creditor action from the scheme rule is to contact the debtor so they make funds available; check whether pre-notification was sent on time. Note: this is scheme guidance, not team guidance.
customer_message: A direct debit collection was returned by the payer's bank because the payer's account did not have enough funds to cover it. Please contact us so we can help you decide on next steps for collecting this payment.

what_happened: AM05 (duplication) on this SEPA Direct Debit return means the clearing system or the debtor's bank treated the collection as a duplicate of an identical one sent very recently, after the funds had settled and come back. The EPC names a technical or human error at the creditor or creditor's bank as the root cause, so this is a system-side check.
next_step: Team guidance: verify whether the collection was really duplicated by checking for an identical collection sent or processed very recently, and confirm the return came through the same clearing system as the original collection. Route to the developer team as the routing table specifies.
customer_message: Your direct debit was returned after it had been processed. The payment was flagged as a possible duplicate, and we are checking the details. We will contact you if we need anything from you.

what_happened: MD01 means the debtor's bank found no valid direct debit mandate, or the debtor disputed the collection as unauthorised. The code alone does not show which MD01 situation applies (no mandate, unconfirmed B2B mandate, bank could not obtain B2B mandate, mandate cancelled after 36 months without collections, or an SDD Core unauthorised-refund request). This is a return after settlement, so the funds were moved and came back.
next_step: Route to Platform support (FIRST_LINE) to resolve with the customer. Review the collection's mandate reference and mandate details against the mandate on file, and check whether it is SDD Core or B2B. If the debtor has requested a refund, contact the debtor as the scheme suggests.
customer_message: A direct debit collection from your account was returned with the reason 'no valid mandate'. Our team is reviewing the mandate details for this collection and will contact you to work out next steps.

what_happened: MD06 means the debtor (payer) exercised their unconditional right to a refund of an authorised SDD Core collection, which can be requested up to 8 weeks after the debit date. The refund can arrive weeks after the collection appeared successful. The route is FIRST_LINE, so platform support resolves it with the creditor.
next_step: Platform support should contact the creditor to explain the MD06 refund request and check whether the pre-notified amount matches the amount collected, since a mismatch is one possible trigger. The scheme guidance suggests the creditor contact the debtor. A person decides the action.
customer_message: A refund request has been made by the payer for a SEPA Direct Debit collection you received. We are reviewing this with you and will confirm the next steps.

what_happened: MS02 means the debtor (payer) refused this SEPA Direct Debit collection after it was presented, typically after receiving the pre-notification, and gave no reason. The decision came from the debtor, not from their bank, and the funds moved and were returned after settlement.
next_step: Route to Platform support (FIRST_LINE), who resolve it with the customer. Per the scheme rule, the suggested creditor action is to contact the debtor; no reason is available from the other bank. This is a recommendation for the operations agent to decide.
customer_message: Your direct debit collection was returned with the reason code MS02. The payer refused the payment and no reason was given. Please get in touch with our platform support team if you would like to discuss next steps or contact the payer directly.

what_happened: MS03 means the debtor's bank returned this SEPA Direct Debit without a specific reason. The EPC allows MS03 only where national law, such as data-protection law, forbids the precise codes, so the underlying cause is unknown and could be one of several. The payment moved and came back, so this is a return after settlement.
next_step: Per the scheme guidance for MS03, contact the debtor (the payer) to find out why the collection was returned. This is a scheme rule, not team guidance. Do not share possible causes with the customer, since the reason was withheld on purpose. A person on the team decides and acts.
customer_message: Your direct debit collection was returned by the payer's bank. The bank did not give a reason. You may wish to contact the payer directly to discuss the payment. We will keep you updated on any further information we receive.

what_happened: RR04 means the debtor's bank stopped this SEPA Direct Debit collection for a possible regulatory reason such as an AML, sanctions or counter-terrorist-financing hit; the funds moved and were returned after settlement. The route is COMPLIANCE, so the compliance team owns the case.
next_step: Hand to Compliance. Do not contact the customer about the reason; Compliance decides what, if anything, is said.

what_happened: AC03 means the creditor (recipient) account number is invalid or missing, per the ISO 20022 definition. This RTP payment was rejected before settlement, so no money moved. The route is FIRST_LINE, so platform support resolves it with the customer.
next_step: Team guidance, not a scheme rule: ask the customer to confirm the recipient's account number directly with the recipient before sending a new payment, and do not resubmit with the same details. If several AC03 rejections hit the same saved payee, check whether the customer's saved payee details are wrong.
customer_message: Your recent payment was rejected because the recipient's account number could not be matched. No money was moved. Please confirm the recipient's account number directly with them before you send a new payment.

what_happened: AC04 means the recipient's account number has been closed on the books of the bank that holds it, so the RTP payment was rejected before settlement and no money moved. This is a closed-account rejection, not a payer-side error.
next_step: Per team guidance (KB-RTP-AC04-01), route this to first-line platform support to resolve with the customer. Do not retry the payment to the same account, and do not suggest the recipient's bank made an error.
customer_message: Your payment was not completed because the recipient's account has been closed, so no money was taken from your account. To proceed, please contact the recipient and ask them for current account details, then start a new payment using those details.

what_happened: AC06 means the receiving party's account is blocked for transactions, so the RTP payment was rejected before settlement and no money moved. Per the ISO 20022 definition, the account is blocked against posting, and the reason is not for us to determine. This is a FIRST_LINE case handled by platform support with the customer.
next_step: Team guidance: have platform support contact the customer, explain that the recipient's account cannot accept this payment, and suggest they agree another account or payment method with the recipient. Do not investigate or share why the account is blocked; that belongs to the recipient's bank.
customer_message: Your payment to the recipient could not be completed because the recipient's account is currently unable to accept payments. No money was moved. You may want to agree another account or payment method with the recipient before trying again.

what_happened: AG01 on this RTP payment means the transaction is forbidden on this type of account, so it was rejected before settlement and no money moved. The route is DEVELOPER, so the developer team should first check whether our configuration or message content caused the rejection.
next_step: Per team guidance (not a scheme rule), the developer team should first check whether anything on our side, such as configuration or message content, caused the rejection. If nothing is wrong on our side, first line can ask the customer to agree another payment method with the recipient.
customer_message: Your payment to the recipient was not completed because this type of transaction is not allowed on your account. No money was taken from your account. You may want to agree another payment method with the recipient.

what_happened: RTP reason code AM04 (Insufficient Funds) means the funds available were insufficient to cover the message amount. The payment was rejected before settlement, so no money moved. The route is Treasury, which handles bank liquidity or prefunded balance issues, so the cause may be on our side rather than the customer's.
next_step: Route this to Treasury to check our bank's own RTP funding position before anyone contacts the customer. Team guidance: do not tell the customer they lack funds unless Treasury confirms the cause was on the customer's side.
customer_message: Your payment of the requested amount could not be completed and was not sent. We are looking into the cause and will update you. Please do not resend the payment until you hear from us.

what_happened: DS24 on this RTP payment means the waiting time expired because the order was incomplete, so the payment timed out and was not completed. The stage is REJECT, so no money moved. The routing table sends this case to the developer team to check connection and processing logs.
next_step: Team guidance, not a scheme rule: before anyone resends, confirm the original payment's final status with a pacs.028 status request to avoid a duplicate payment. Route to the developer team for review of connection and processing logs.
customer_message: Your payment did not complete. Please don't send it again until we've confirmed its status.

what_happened: RR04 means the receiving bank stopped this RTP payment for a regulatory reason, such as a possible AML, sanctions or counter-terrorist-financing hit. The payment was rejected before settlement and no funds moved. The route is COMPLIANCE, so this is for the compliance team to review.
next_step: Hand to Compliance. Do not contact the customer about the reason; Compliance decides what, if anything, is said.

what_happened: The payment was flagged as possibly fraudulent.
next_step: Pass to the fraud team immediately. Do not retry, refund or contact the other party until the fraud team decides.
customer_message: We are reviewing this payment. Please contact us if you have any questions.
note: No guidance available: showing the baseline for this code (D7).

what_happened: Reason code CNOR is not in our code table.
next_step: Escalate for manual triage; no explanation is available for this code.

what_happened: No failure to explain: the payment was accepted or settled.
No failure to explain yet: the payment is still pending. Do not resend; wait for the final status or request it (pacs.028 status request).
The other bank rejected or returned the payment because the other party's account is blocked.
next_step: Tell the customer the other party's account cannot receive or pay this transaction, and suggest they agree another account or payment method with the other party. Do not speculate about why it is blocked.
customer_message: Your payment could not be completed because the other party's account cannot accept it. Please contact them to agree another way to pay.
note: No guidance available: showing the baseline for this code (D7).

what_happened: AC04 means the beneficiary's account is closed at the beneficiary's bank, so the payment was rejected before settlement and no money moved. Our customer is the payer, and the beneficiary is the party whose account is closed. The scheme suggests the payer contact the beneficiary to obtain their new account details.
next_step: Route to Platform support (FIRST_LINE) to resolve with the customer. Suggest the customer contact the beneficiary directly to get a current account. Note that some SEPA countries send MS03 instead of AC04 for the same situation, so the cause may not be stated precisely.
customer_message: Your SEPA Instant payment was not completed because the beneficiary's account could not be found as open at their bank. No money has left your account. You may wish to contact the person or business you were paying to confirm their current account details, then send the payment again.
